When there is no AC power
column2: NIC may not work after changing mac address.

column1: This issue is caused by runtime power management. When there is no AC

column2: if we put NIC down (ifconfig down)
column3: the driver will be in runtime

column1: suspend state and hardware will be put into D3 state. During this time
driver cannot access hardware regisers. So if you set new mac address

column2: it will not be set to hardware. After resume

column1: keep using the old mac address and the network will not work normally.
In this patch I add detecting runtime pm status when setting mac address.
If driver is in runtime suspend state
column2: it will skip setting mac address
and set the new mac address during runtime resume.
